extraction.name: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI
extraction.description: A benchmark of 11.5K college-level multimodal questions spanning 6 disciplines, 30 subjects, and 183 subfields, curated from college exams, quizzes, textbooks, online sources, and lecture materials to evaluate multimodal understanding and reasoning.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.citeAs: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark collection took three stages: first, the authors selected subjects from common university majors based on whether visual inputs are commonly used; second, over 50 university students including co-authors collected multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources and created new questions where necessary; third, the authors cleaned duplicates, checked format and typos, and categorized difficulty levels, excluding about 10% of very easy problems.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper explicitly notes that annotators were advised to select questions without immediately available answers, such as those with answers in separate documents or at the end of textbooks.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: College exams, quizzes, textbooks, online resources, lecture materials, and other study materials.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Potential duplicates were identified using lexical overlap and source URL similarity and then removed after author review; problems were distributed among co-authors for format and typo checking; authors categorized problems into difficulty levels and excluded approximately 10% of very easy problems that did not fit the design criteria.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Duplicate removal, format and typo checking, difficulty categorization, and exclusion of approximately 10% of very easy problems not aligned with the benchmark design criteria.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, collected multimodal questions from textbooks and online resources and created new questions when necessary. They were instructed to follow copyright and license regulations, avoid prohibited sources, avoid questions with immediately available answers, and ensure questions were college-level, unambiguous, in English, and contained one or more images. A secondary review team vetted annotations, and random audits were conducted.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A user-friendly web interface for data annotation and verification was developed.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper reports quality control through duplicate detection, author review, format and typo checking, difficulty labeling, secondary review, and random audits. It also discusses data contamination considerations by avoiding questions with easily accessible answers.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the relevant majors; 90 college senior students were used as human experts for evaluation.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Lexical overlap and source URL similarity were used for duplicate detection; OCR by MMOCR and captioning by LLaVA-1.5 were used in evaluation baselines, but not as annotation tools.
